question.problem:
Let $V={R}_{2}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $2,$ equipped with the inner product 

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(0)y(0)+x(1)y(1)+\frac{1}{10}x(2)y(2).
$$

If $p(t)=3+t$ and $q(t)=3t-k{t}^{2}$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
question.worked_solution:
Since $p(t)$ and $q(t)$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =p(0)q(0)+2p(1)q(1)+\frac{1}{10}p(2)q(2) \\  & =(3+0)(0)+(3+1)(3-k)+\frac{1}{10}(3+2)(6-4k) \\  & =0+(12-4k)+(3-2k) \\  & =15-6k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨p(t),q(t)⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),q(t)⟩ & =0 \\ 15-6k & =0 \\ 6k & =15 \\ k & =\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
